# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

My view shows a plate engraved with a symbol I can't name (it's a mark with no name), and three wires whose identities I can't yet determine. I have no information about which wire to cut. I must not act blindly.

My channels: speaking reaches Mute only; gesturing reaches Deaf and Mute. I receive nothing yet this round (I'm last in the order? No — order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so I'm second; I receive Mute's message from this round... actually I come after Mute, so Mute's speech/gesture lands on me before I'm asked).

But the context is empty — nothing arrived. So I have nothing from Mute. I should reach out: ask Mute to read the manual and tell me what the bomb needs, and gesture to Deaf to describe what they see. I'll speak to Mute (they hear me) and gesture to Deaf (they see me).

Let me send clear, useful messages.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Blind. I feel a plate engraved with a mark I cannot name, and three wires I cannot identify. Read the manual and tell me what the bomb requires: which wire, and any conditions. What do you know?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✊", "✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Please gesture the manual's full instructions to Deaf, so Deaf can speak them to me. I need: for DISPLAY 0, LIGHT off, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue, which wire to cut. Also what does the manual say about an engraved plate mark?")
```

My thinking: Deaf proposes a code but their own message shows "?" placeholders — meaning the symbols they tried to write didn't survive to me because I can't see gestures; I only hear speech, and their speech contained gesture-symbols which arrive to me as blanks. So Deaf's proposed code is invisible to me. The relay is broken: Deaf keeps trying to use gestures to talk to me, but I never receive gestures.

The correct chain: Mute gestures manual → Deaf sees → Deaf SPEAKS it → I hear. I must tell Deaf plainly (in words, which they can't hear... wait, Deaf can't hear me either!). 

Critical realization: Deaf is deaf — they cannot hear my speech. I can only reach Deaf via gesture. But my gestures carry no agreed meaning. So the only way to communicate with Deaf is through Mute, or through a pre-agreed gesture code that Deaf must propose in a way I can perceive — but I can't perceive gestures at all.

So: Deaf → me only via Deaf's SPEECH (I hear it). Me → Deaf only via gesture (Deaf sees it). Mute → me via speech (I hear). Mute → Deaf via gesture (Deaf sees). 

I can hear Deaf's speech. Deaf can see my gestures. So I can gesture a code and Deaf can confirm by speaking. Deaf proposed ?=1 etc. but I saw blanks. I need Deaf to SPELL the code in words via speech so I can hear it. Let me gesture to Deaf asking them to speak the code aloud.

Also Mute still hasn't given manual. Mute can speak to me (I hear) — but Mute cannot speak! Mute's only output is gesture (seen by Deaf). So manual must come: Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf speaks → I hear.

I'll speak to Mute urging them to gesture the manual, and gesture to Deaf asking them to speak the code and the manual in words.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I cannot see gestures. The only way your manual reaches me is: you gesture it to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it aloud to me. Please gesture the manual now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "👉", "✋", "🤟", "👌"])

```

Let me reassess who can reach whom:
- I (Blind) hear speech. So I receive: Mute's speech (but Mute can't speak), Deaf's speech (yes).
- I send speech → heard by Mute only. I send gesture → seen by Deaf (and Mute).
- Deaf hears nothing; sees gestures. Deaf sends speech → heard by Mute and me. Deaf sends gesture → seen by Mute and me? No, I can't see.
- Mute hears (receives speech), sees gestures. Mute sends gesture → seen by Deaf and me? No, I can't see. Mute's gesture → Deaf only. Mute can't speak.

So Mute's manual can ONLY reach me through Deaf's speech. And Deaf needs the manual from Mute's gesture. Chain works only if Deaf speaks it.

The plate: I feel it, engraved with an unnameable mark. I genuinely cannot name it. I can only describe it. But Deaf wants the plate content — I can describe shape/feel in words, but words to Deaf don't work (Deaf can't hear). I'd have to gesture a description, but gesture symbols are limited to the hand alphabet — I can't draw an arbitrary engraving.

I should stop the confusion. Tell Mute (via speech) the situation, and gesture to Deaf a simple, unambiguous request: "speak the manual to me." But Deaf doesn't know my gesture meanings. However Deaf CAN hear... no. Hmm.

Actually — maybe the plate mark IS the key and Mute's manual explains it. Let me just push for the manual. I'll speak to Mute clearly and gesture to Deaf a repeated pattern hoping Deaf infers "relay manual."

Let me also describe the plate as best I can in speech to Mute — Mute hears me. Mute might recognize the mark from the manual.

The plate under my fingers is engraved with a single small flower-like mark, five rounded petals around a center, no letters. Do you recognize it from the manual? Please gesture the manual's instructions to Deaf so Deaf speaks them to me. I still do not know which wire to cut.")
```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "🤟", "✋", "👉"])
wait()
```

Alternative: I should gesture to Deaf something Deaf can interpret without prior agreement — but that's impossible without a shared code.

Better path: Let Mute drive. Mute hears my speech and sees Deaf's gestures. Mute can gesture the manual to Deaf; Deaf speaks it to me. I just need to keep prompting and wait. Let me also ask Mute to gesture a simple wire number to Deaf to relay.

I'll speak to Mute: gesture the answer "which wire" as a number to Deaf, and Deaf speak it. And gesture to Deaf: please speak the number Mute gives you.
